lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: These show the old bookshop and three nearby stores. What if we save more neighborhood photos and short stories before they disappear?

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: We could create a small then-and-now exhibit. I have recent photos of several of these streets.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: I like the idea, but I'm not sure thirty photo pairs and recorded interviews will be manageable for our first event.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I feel disappointed when good material stays in boxes, but I don't need everything displayed at once.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: Then let's keep it manageable: twelve photo pairs and up to six short written stories.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: That might work. We can use one wall at the arts center if the dates and permissions are clear.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Some owners are unknown. We're not committing to public display yet.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: The first step is to check the space, contributors and image permissions.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: I'll contact two former neighbors, but I won't promise that their stories will be used.

lines.speaker: Daniel
lines.text: I'll select twelve candidate pairs. They're only candidates until everyone agrees.

lines.speaker: Lena
lines.text: I'll check two early-fall Saturdays. Let's make sure everyone agrees before we announce a date.

lines.speaker: Grace
lines.text: Good. If those checks work, we move ahead with a small exhibit—not a huge festival.
